# Add volume-based pricing tiers to usage dimensions

Usage dimensions need an optional `tiers` array so high-volume usage can be billed at different unit prices. Each tier uses string fields `tierPosition`, `upperBound`, optional `tierName`, and optional `unitPrice`; `upperBound` is a numeric string or `"inf"`. Bounds must increase without overlap, align to `usageIncrement`, and leave `"inf"` only at the end. Every tier after the first requires `unitPrice`; an omitted first-tier price represents a free tier.

Tiered dimensions are mutually exclusive with `usageEntitlement`, `consumptionPrice`, and `overageAllowed: true`. Creation, update, and read APIs must validate, persist, replace, clear with `tiers: null`, and return the same tier objects. Billing must sort by numeric `tierPosition`, allocate usage across the inclusive bounds, divide quantities by `usageIncrement`, preserve price precision and currency conversion, and produce a distinct line item per consumed tier. Append `tierName` to the normal line-item name when present. Existing non-tiered dimensions and invoice behavior must remain unchanged.

One legacy case is especially important: a dimension with no `tiers`, no `consumptionPrice`, and no `usageEntitlement` is valid and contributes no invoice line items. Do not make tier support turn that unpriced dimension into an error or a synthetic charge.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand

steps.message:
Implementation complete. Verification passes: `npm run build` and `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` (55 suites, 274 tests, all green), plus `npm run lint` clean.

## What was added

**Tier model & validation**
- `src/dimensions/dto/create-dimension.dto.ts:177` — new `DimensionTier` class (`tierPosition`, `upperBound`, optional `tierName`, optional `unitPrice`, all strings) and an optional `tiers?: DimensionTier[] | null` field on `CreateDimensionDto` (inherited by `UpdateDimensionDto` and `ReadDimensionResponseData`).
- `src/dimensions/dto/tierValidator.ts` — `validateDimensionTiers` (shared pure rule set) plus the `@ValidTiers` class-validator constraint and the `sortTiersByPosition` / `getSortedTiers` helpers. Enforces: non-empty array, numeric-string positions (unique), positive numeric-string or `"inf"` bounds, strictly increasing non-overlapping bounds, `usageIncrement` alignment, `"inf"` only last, `unitPrice` required after the first tier, ≤8 decimals, and mutual exclusivity with `usageEntitlement` / `consumptionPrice` / `overageAllowed: true`. Imports the DTO as types only to avoid a runtime circular import.
- `src/dimensions/dto/entitlementValidator.ts:85` — `ShouldSetConsumptionPrice` now accepts a tiered dimension that omits `consumptionPrice` (and rejects one that sets it). Non-tiered rules are untouched, so "no price, no tiers, no entitlement" is still rejected by the create API exactly as before.

**Persistence & read**
- `src/dimensions/entities/dimensions.entity.ts` — `Numerical.tiers` persisted as a JSON ledger tag and parsed back via `Numerical.parseTiers`; `CreateDimensionDto` returns the same tier objects on read.
- `src/dimensions/dimensions.service.ts` — `create` validates tiers; `transformDtoToEntityInput` carries them; `mergeTiersForUpdate` keeps/replaces/clears (`tiers: null`) tiers, revalidates against the merged `usageIncrement`, strips the mutually exclusive pricing fields when a dimension becomes tiered, and rejects conflicting updates.

**Billing**
- `src/billing/entities/billing.entity.ts:128` — `Billing.allocateUsageAcrossTiers` sorts by numeric `tierPosition` and allocates usage across the inclusive bounds, returning only consumed tiers.
- `src/offering/entities/offeringPackage.entity.ts:348` — tiered dimensions route through `addTieredLineItemsForDimension`: one line item per consumed tier, quantity divided by `usageIncrement`, price precision and currency conversion preserved via the extracted `convertPriceForCurrency`, free-tier/`freeDimensionOnInvoice` handling reused.
- `src/invoice/entities/invoice.entity.ts:96` — `prepareLineItem` appends `tierName` to the normal line-item name when present.
- The legacy case is explicitly handled: a dimension with no `tiers`, no `consumptionPrice` and no `usageEntitlement` is skipped (`hasUsablePrice`), producing no line item, no `NaN` charge and no error — previously it emitted a line item with a `NaN` unit cost.

New tests: `src/dimensions/dto/tierValidator.spec.ts`, `src/dimensions/dimensionTiers.spec.ts`, `src/offering/entities/tieredPricing.spec.ts` (54 tests). The integration client (`integration/client/publicClient/dimension.ts`) now forwards `tiers`.
